decision: Introduce a distinct 'bash-stage' ToolCategory for git add (true in EXECUTING+FINALIZING) instead of moving git add into the commit set
alternatives: move git add to GIT_COMMIT_SUBCOMMANDS as originally specified; keep git add unchanged
reasoning: Live probe: state.json ownerSessionId=4a3a403f equals THIS subagent session id, and a Bash call from this subagent was BLOCKED as bash-mutate in PLANNING. Subagents inherit owner session_id and are NOT bystander-exempt. Moving git add to the commit set would newly BLOCK bare git add in EXECUTING (bash-commit:false), tightening a path executors use today. A distinct staging category fixes FINALIZING without regressing EXECUTING.
risk: Adds a ToolCategory column; every matrix row must be updated or tsc fails (compile-time, not runtime)

decision: Widen TMP_FILE_RE to accept .md alongside .json rather than changing finalize.ts to stage the PR body as .json
alternatives: change the finalize instruction to write .luca/tmp/pr-body-draft.json
reasoning: A PR body is markdown; forcing it into .json would require JSON-encoding prose at author time and decoding at gh pr create time. TMP_FILE_RE guards an inert gitignored scratch dir, so widening it to .md is a negligible grant. Instruction-body edits also only reach users after build+luca init, so fixing the regex takes effect immediately for existing installs.
risk: Widens an ephemeral-path allow; mitigated by keeping the regex anchored to .luca/tmp/<kebab-name>.(json|md) with no path traversal

decision: Retarget D5: keep 'rules' in LUCA_TOPLEVEL_READ and fix the false prose in finalize.ts instead of reclassifying the noun as a write
alternatives: move rules into LUCA_TOPLEVEL_WRITE as context.md D2.4 specified; move it and add a compensating WRITE_COMMAND_PHASES entry
reasoning: context.md asserts 'luca rules suggest' writes draft .luca/rules/*.ts. Verified false: rules.ts:122-134 calls process.stdout.write only, with zero writeFile/Bun.write/mkdir calls in the file; all four rules verbs are read-only. LUCA_TOPLEVEL_READ/WRITE are keyed by NOUN, so moving it would reclassify three unrelated read verbs. The compensating WRITE_COMMAND_PHASES key would be inert because rulesCommand is a plain citty defineCommand that never routes through runWriteHandler. The false claim lives in the instruction body (finalize.ts:21,286) - same defect class as D3.
risk: Reinterprets a user-decided scope item; user should confirm. If the intent was to ADD a rule-writing capability, that is new CLI surface and out of scope per the phase constraints.

decision: Renumber SEVERITY so bash-stage is strictly below bash-mutate, not merely below bash-commit
alternatives: insert bash-stage at the existing tier 1 alongside bash-mutate and luca-write
reasoning: maxCategory is SEVERITY[a] >= SEVERITY[b] ? a : b (classify-bash-command.ts:384-386), so ties keep the FIRST-seen operand. A tier-1 tie would make 'git add . && rm -rf build' classify as bash-stage, which is allowed in FINALIZING where bash-mutate is denied — laundering an arbitrary mutation into the phase this work is widening. Verified the operator is >= not > by reading the source.
risk: Renumbering SEVERITY shifts luca-write/bash-mutate/bash-commit tier values; any code comparing raw SEVERITY numbers rather than using maxCategory would need review

decision: Pin the SEVERITY renumber as a five-relation ordering invariant (ac-21.1-21.5 + anti-09) rather than the single bash-stage < bash-mutate relation, explicitly preserving luca-write === bash-mutate
alternatives: pin only bash-stage < bash-mutate as originally written
reasoning: The shared luca-write/bash-mutate tier is deliberate and documented in-source at classify-bash-command.ts:374-377. A renumber inserting bash-stage at 1 and bumping only bash-mutate to 2 satisfies the single-relation check while silently flipping 'luca checks run && rm -f x' from luca-write (legal in every non-IDLE phase) to bash-mutate (denied in PLANNING/REVIEWING/FINALIZING) - the same tightening class bash-stage exists to avoid. Verified SEVERITY has exactly one consumer (maxCategory at :385); DEFAULT_SEVERITY_RANK in luca-core is unrelated, so blast radius is a single expression.
risk: Five ordering criteria plus an export make the task heavier; mitigated because the target map is fully specified in the task text (readonly:0, stage:1, luca-write:2, mutate:2, commit:3, denied:4)

decision: Match .changeset/<name>.md with a segment-anchored regex plus a README.md negative lookahead, rather than a .changeset/* glob
alternatives: explicit deny-list of README.md and config.json checked after a broad match
reasoning: Plan required README.md and config.json to stay 'code' (ac-02/ac-03) and a nested/non-md path to stay 'code' (anti-02). A single anchored regex requiring .md, forbidding a slash in the name, and excluding README.md satisfies all three without a second pass. Segment anchoring also handles the ABSOLUTE file_path Claude Code passes.
risk: A future changesets convention using a non-.md release-note file would silently fall back to 'code' and be blocked in FINALIZING — a fail-closed direction, not fail-open.
reviewHint: Confirm the release-artifact grant in EXECUTING is intended (it preserves today's code-write:true), not scope creep.

decision: Placed the git-add bash-stage branch after GIT_COMMIT check and before GIT_MUTATE check, modeled on the mutate branch (lastNonFlag target extraction); removed 'add' from GIT_MUTATE_SUBCOMMANDS; renumbered SEVERITY wholesale with bash-stage at tier 1 strictly below the shared luca-write/bash-mutate tier 2
alternatives: bump only bash-mutate (breaks luca-write shared tier)
reasoning: Plan traps 1-3 dictate exact shape; mutate-branch template preserves target extraction the always-denied path check consumes; wholesale SEVERITY renumber preserves luca-write===bash-mutate tier while placing bash-stage strictly below
risk: A future git subcommand named differently could bypass; bash-stage tie-with-mutate would launder mutations into FINALIZING (pinned by anti-07)
reviewHint: Verify bash-stage strictly below bash-mutate in SEVERITY and that git-add branch precedes the mutate check

decision: Encoded completeness invariant as per-pair test.each over LUCA_NOUN_VERBS write verbs, keyed as `${noun} ${verb}` to match WRITE_COMMAND_PHASES space-separated keys
alternatives: per-noun test.each with array coverage assertion
reasoning: Per-pair test.each names the exact violating <noun> <verb> in the failure diff, mirroring the file's existing invariant-1 style; space-key format matches every non-read entry in the luca-core table
risk: branch-guard uses a hyphen key but branch/guard verb is a read verb (exempt), so no false negative
